knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says not to sniff, taste or combine chemicals to identify them, and to isolate and escalate unknown residues. Smell is not a safe identification method.
The closure step records the instruction received and who gave it, and work resumes only when it is safe. A customer's opinion is not the hazard decision.
The recognise decision triggers section says to separate routine service questions from hazards, injuries, suspected abuse, aggressive behaviour, unexpected contamination and unauthorised work.

practicalCriteria: Learner completes procedure step 1: Sort the issue into a routine service question or a hazard, injury, suspected abuse, aggressive behaviour, unexpected contamination or unauthorised work, using the organisation's escalation matrix.
Learner completes procedure step 2: Pause any task that is beyond your competence or control.
Learner completes procedure step 3: Secure the area only if it is safe to do so. Avoid disturbing evidence or attempting specialist clean-up.
Learner completes procedure step 4: For immediate danger, contact emergency services. For other safety issues, contact the designated supervisor or site contact.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 5: For suspected harm to a vulnerable person, follow the organisation's safeguarding reporting procedure and the applicable law.

Record of procedure step 6: Give a factual report stating who, where, what you observed, the immediate risks, the actions already taken and the support required. Keep observations separate from assumptions.
Record of procedure step 7: Do not resume work because a customer says a hazard is probably harmless. Resume only after the designated supervisor or site contact gives a recorded instruction.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Sort the issue into a routine service question or a hazard, injury, suspected abuse, aggressive behaviour, unexpected contamination or unauthorised work, using the organisation's escalation matrix.

Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: Do not resume work because a customer says a hazard is probably harmless. Resume only after the designated supervisor or site contact gives a recorded instruction.
Stop work if procedure step 8 is not done: Record the instruction received, the responsible person, the time and whether work may safely resume. Escalate again if conditions change.
